data.narrative:
Critical Energy, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Spencer Jackson, has raised $22M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 firms in the Climate & Energy sector—1 public (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix—though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within this cohort proved insufficient for reliable peer-median triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable quantitative approach, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage transitions. Using the $22M total raised as a valuation proxy, this yields an implied value of $55M. Given the limited methodological inputs and inherent uncertainty around stage-progression timing and company-specific progression risk, a conservative range of $47M to $63M reflects reasonable bounds around the central estimate.

The analysis supports a median valuation of $55M, with key uncertainties centered on the absence of direct peer-stage comparables and the timing and terms of the next financing round. Investors should weight this estimate heavily against company-specific metrics—burn rate, product-market fit signals, and capital efficiency relative to the broader Climate & Energy landscape—before making final valuation judgments.
